facts.fact: 姐姐（此句原文拼作 Keilin）两天前被告知静玲在岛上某家妓院做工；两天的愤怒、不信、最后是好奇，强到她要亲自去看。注意：同一人在本章另有拼写 Kiamling，指的是同一个姐姐。
facts.anchor: It had been two days since Keilin had told her about Jingling working in one of the brothels on the island. Two days of anger, disbelief and finally curiosity, overwhelming enough that she had to see for herself.

facts.fact: 太平山街上一名穿昂贵长袍、浑身 mau toi 浓香的商人（先前从背后抓住她肩膀，她手已按剑柄）好奇地问她：「你是男孩还是女孩」。
facts.anchor: The cloying smell of mau toi lingered around his expensive robes. Curious, he asked, “Are you a boy or a girl?”

facts.fact: 她当机立断，在街上一家花店买了一抱鲜花，连篮子一并买下；用意是让花色引开对脸和身子的注意，使自己「有东西可卖」。
facts.anchor: Kiamling thought fast, stopping at one of the many flower shops to buy an armful of blooms, the basket too.

facts.fact: 她给自己定下的目的与规矩：至少要看一眼妹妹做工的地方、查看是否安全、员工有无受虐；这回她对自己发誓不闹事（上一回已让妹妹难堪）。
facts.anchor: but if Jingling was working at a brothel, she at least needed to see the place. Check its safety, that staff were not being mistreated. This time, she vowed to herself, she wouldn’t cause a scene.

facts.fact: 最气派的那家最好认：街面中段的大楼，金红二色招牌写着 Pavilion of Spring Buds（春芽阁）；她嫌名字晦涩，讥道「不如干脆叫鸡笼」。
facts.anchor: The most opulent brothel was easy to spot: that would be the huge building that sat in the middle of the row. A sign painted in gold and red declared it to be the Pavilion of Spring Buds

facts.fact: 门口一名女子收下她一支花、拉动门上的黄铜环替她开门，并催她快进去、别让妈妈桑看见，还祝两人今晚生意都好——是这名妓女放她进的门，不是老鸨。
facts.anchor: “Go on in, little sister, quick, before the madam sees you. I wish us both good business tonight.”

facts.fact: 妓院也设神龛，供的是花艇与妓馆之神 Bak Mei San；Por Por 本人曾在太平山街接活，但从不许 Kiamling 跟着去。这是姐姐对这行的旧识来源。
facts.anchor: They too had shrines, to Bak Mei San, god of flower boats and pleasure houses. Por Por had taken on jobs in Tai Ping Shan Street; she had just declined to ever let Kiamling accompany her.

facts.fact: 她认出撞到她、用英文骂「Mind where you are going!」的人是 Francis Peake——总督秘书、鬼节演出时坐前排的人之一；他领结松垮、下巴沾白粉，显然刚上过包房；她举花篮遮脸兜售，他慌忙找借口走人。
facts.anchor: She had recognised him. Francis Peake, secretary to the governor, one of those who had sat in the front row during the Ghost Festival performance.

facts.fact: 老鸨登场：Madam Yau Yuhuan（本章唯一给出的全名），全场最夺目的女人，比多数男人（连欧人在内）都高；众妓女立刻围上递热毛巾、斟茶、帮她解斗篷。
facts.anchor: It was the madam of the house. Madam Yau Yuhuan was the most striking woman Kiamling had ever met. Taller than most men, even the Europeans

facts.fact: 她背上绑着一个布结长包裹，长度与体积足以藏下武器——这是姐姐起疑的物证之一。
facts.anchor: Strapped to her back was a fabric-knotted bundle, long and bulky enough to conceal a weapon.

facts.fact: 静玲登台时穿翡翠绿上衣，领口与宽袖镶黑底花边，下身同色裙；这身打扮不像姐妹平日装束，更近戏子行头（同段末句：头发挽成低髻）。
facts.anchor: Jingling wore a beautiful emerald-green top, a contrasting black floral border around the collar and wide sleeves, with a matching skirt beneath.

facts.fact: 静玲左侧发间垂着珠串，插的正是 Kiamling 送她的那支发簪；她仍戴着，姐姐因此认定关系还有修补余地、胸中涌起希望。
facts.anchor: On the left side of her head, beads dangled from a familiar hair stick: the one Kiamling had bought her.

facts.fact: 自毁的一念推翻了和解的设想：她只来看妹妹做什么工，不是来认错；既认定妹妹不需要她，她这做姐姐的也不必需要妹妹，遂趁静玲目光未及先躲开。
facts.anchor: A self-destructive streak obliterated the image. She was only here to see what sort of work Jingling engaged in, not as an admission of wrongdoing.

facts.fact: Madam Yau 把包裹放到办公桌上，一边解结一边说话，说「我们安全了」；这句像对屋里另一个人说的，但全章没有任何回应——姐姐等的是开箱或有人推屏风，落空。
facts.anchor: Madam Yau had placed her parcel down on the desk and was talking as she undid the knots. “We’re safe now.”

facts.fact: 包裹里是四把破旧纸伞；她在室内、且当日整日干燥的情况下仍撑开一把，盐状粉末从竹骨簌簌落下，洒在她头上、在地面积成一堆——撑伞撒粉的是 Madam Yau 本人。
facts.anchor: Inside the parcel were four tattered paper umbrellas. She opened one of them over her head, despite being inside, despite the weather having been dry all day.

facts.fact: 白粉闪光、嘶嘶化烟、盘旋成女人形状：形销骨立、皮紧贴骨、颈长可回头、嘴细长如补针、双眼全白无瞳、黑发垂腰、白袍溅血、通体透明；姐姐判定这是 lui gwei——复仇女鬼。
facts.anchor: All of this was clear to Kiamling, even though the woman’s outline flickered and she was entirely transparent. It was a lui gwei. A vengeful female ghost.
